raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

On Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-FP8 (TP4, EAGLE, MI355X), decode in the 20261008 image is 1–3% slower than the 20260929 image at batch 8 to 64. The gap is a fixed cost of about 0.4–0.6 ms per cycle, so it is largest at small batches. A 30-step profile at batch 8 shows a `compare_scalar` kernel that the old image does not have: 45 launches per cycle, about 0.34 ms, between `fused_qkvzba_split_reshape_cat` and `causal_conv1d_update`.

#### Root cause

#40001 added `select_verify_intermediate_state_indices()` for pipeline-parallel speculative decoding. The helper returns the default indices immediately unless `SGLANG_ENABLE_PP_SPEC` is on. The GDN and KDA verify paths still pass `cache_indices[: query_start_loc.shape[0] - 1] >= 0` as an argument, so Python builds that mask before the helper can discard it. Each linear-attention layer launches one compare kernel per speculative verify step, and the result is thrown away. Qwen3.5 has 45 of these layers. This recipe does not enable PP x speculative decoding.

This PR does not change the indices. It stops building the mask unless the flag is on.

## Modifications

- `gdn_backend.py`: in `GDNAttnBackend` target verify, keep `verify_intermediate_state_indices` unless `pp_spec_stable_rows_enabled()`. Only then call `select_verify_intermediate_state_indices()` with the compare. With the flag on, the call and its arguments are unchanged.
- `kda_backend.py`: the same guard. KDA is not on the Qwen3.5 path; the call site has the same eager compare.
- `qwen4_exp.py` still builds its mask before the same helper. That path is not used by Qwen3.5 and is not changed here.

## Accuracy Tests

No output change on the default path. With `SGLANG_ENABLE_PP_SPEC` unset, the helper returns `verify_intermediate_state_indices` without reading the mask, and the patched code uses that tensor directly. With the flag set, the helper is called with the same arguments as before.

No separate GSM8K run was collected for this guard.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

### Decode step time

one target pass plus 3 draft passes, CUDA graph on. TP4, `--enable-aiter-allreduce-fusion`, FP8 KV cache. 

- `old` is `lmsysorg/sglang-rocm:v0.5.20-rocm720-mi35x-20260929`. 
- `new` is the 20261006 ROCm 7.2 image with SGLang `943621c` (contains #40001). 
- `pr` is `new` plus this guard. Mean of the runs in parentheses. The fix column is one run.

`pr vs new` is the effect of this guard. `new vs old` and `pr vs old` compare with the 20260929 image.

| Batch | old  (ms/cycle) | new (ms/cycle) | fix (ms/cycle) | new vs old | fix vs new |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 8 | 16.40 | 16.96 | 16.29 | +3.4% | -4.0% |
| 16 | 19.33 | 19.78 | 19.16 | +2.3% | -3.1% |
| 32 | 24.71 | 25.59 | 25.02 | +3.6% | -2.2% |
| 64 | 34.21 | 34.59 | 34.28 | +1.1% | -0.9% |

### AgentX benchmark

- Hardware: MI355X, TP4.
- Model and recipe: `Qwen/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-FP8` on `lmsysorg/sglang-rocm:v0.5.21-rocm720-mi35x-20261008`.
- Server: FP8 KV cache, EAGLE 3 / 1 / 4, simulated acceptance 3.39, and `--enable-aiter-allreduce-fusion`.
- Client: AgentX trace replay on `semianalysis_cc_traces_weka_062126_256k`, 3,600 seconds per run.
- Baseline is the unmodified image; This PR is the same image plus the exact GDN/KDA guard at this PR head. Higher throughput and interactivity are better.

Concurrency 8:

| Metric | Baseline | This PR | Change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Requests completed in 3600 s | 1,499 | 1,498 | ~0 |
| Output throughput (tok/s) | 405.46 | 406.46 | +0.2% |
| Interactivity p50 / p90 (tok/s/user) | 264.93 / 219.25 | 267.49 / 217.13 | +1.0% / -1.0% |
| Total throughput (tok/s/GPU), guardrail | 10,254.57 | 10,203.90 | -0.5% |

Concurrency 32:

| Metric | Baseline | This PR | Change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Requests completed in 3600 s | 4,894 | 4,910 | +0.3% |
| Output throughput (tok/s) | 1,284.83 | 1,293.08 | +0.6% |
| Interactivity p50 / p90 (tok/s/user) | 145.92 / 84.37 | 148.52 / 84.33 | +1.8% / ~0 |
| Total throughput (tok/s/GPU), guardrail | 36,824.65 | 37,059.09 | +0.6% |

Both c32 arms used identical HiCache settings. GPU cache hit rate was 88.7% vs 88.6%, and external cache hit rate was 0.6% in both. All four arms had zero profiled-request errors.

The end-to-end changes are small and mixed: output throughput is flat to +0.6%, while p90 interactivity ranges from -1.0% to unchanged. Treat the AgentX result as neutral within run-to-run variation. The decode-cycle/profile results above remain the direct evidence that the guard removes the unused compare work, while the AgentX shows no end-to-end regression outside that noise band.

## Checklist

- [ ] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). — no user-facing change.
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

## Review and Merge Process

1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process).
2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers.
3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so.
   - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci`
4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR.

nodes.body:
`self.verify_intermediate_state_indices` isn't a flag. It's just the default index table. The actual flag is `SGLANG_ENABLE_PP_SPEC` (off by default). 

Previously, we always built a mask (`cache_indices[...] >= 0`) and passed it to `select_verify_intermediate_state_indices()`. But when `SGLANG_ENABLE_PP_SPEC` is off, that function ignores the mask and just returns the default table, so the mask was a wasted GPU kernel across 45 layers per decode cycle on Qwen3.5. 

Now we only build the mask when `SGLANG_ENABLE_PP_SPEC` is on. When it's off, we use the default table directly, which is the same result as before.

And yes, it's hardware agnostic. It's just a Python-side check, nothing vendor-specific.
